walkthroughs.body_html:
Sports Psychology — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sports Psychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sports Psychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: When you flex your elbow, which muscle is the agonist?
options: Resting heart rate times 4.
Biceps brachii.
Triceps brachii.
Deltoid.

mcqs.q: What is the rough formula for maximum heart rate?
options: 220 minus age (in beats per minute).
When arousal is at minimum.
Age plus 100.
Resting heart rate times 4.

mcqs.q: According to the inverted-U hypothesis, when is performance best?
options: When arousal is at maximum.
At an optimal moderate level of arousal.
Deltoid.
When arousal is at minimum.

mcqs.q: Year of the first modern Olympic Games?

numericals.q: Year of the first modern Olympic Games?

sequence.def: From 776 BC in ancient Greece — the earliest event.
Early 1800s: English public schools codify games.
Mid-1800s: urbanisation and free time reshape sport.
Late 1800s onward: players paid to compete.
Revived in 1896 by Coubertin — the modern era.
